title: Energy Forms and Conversion
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Energy Forms and Conversion Worksheets (PSLE Practice with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 6: Energy forms and uses (Energy conversion)
standard_text: Recognise the different forms of energy: kinetic energy, potential energy (gravitational, elastic and chemical), light, heat, sound and electrical energy. Recognise that energy can be converted from one form to another, that it cannot be created or destroyed, and that the Sun is the main source of energy. Show an understanding of the need to use energy wisely (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on forms of energy and energy conversion: kinetic and potential energy, light, heat, sound and electrical energy. PSLE practice with answers.
key_big: Energy changes form; it is never used up.
key_sub: Kinetic, potential, light, heat, sound and electrical energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy can be converted from one form to another, but it cannot be created or destroyed.

  • Kinetic energy: energy of a moving object.
  • Potential energy: stored energy: gravitational (raised up), elastic (stretched or compressed), chemical (in food, fuels, batteries).
  • Other forms: light, heat, sound and electrical energy.
  • The Sun is the main source of energy for the Earth.
Example

A ball is dropped from a height. What conversion happens?

At the top it has gravitational potential energy

As it falls it speeds up

Answer: Gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy.

Example

Where does the energy in our food come from?

Plants use light to make food

Animals eat plants

Answer: The Sun.

Common mistakes

  • Saying energy is 'used up'. It is converted into other forms, often heat.
  • Thinking an object at rest at a height has no energy. It has gravitational potential energy.
  • Thinking a battery stores electrical energy. It stores chemical potential energy.
  • Mixing up kinetic and potential energy for a stretched rubber band (it has elastic potential energy).

faq.q: What are the forms of energy in Primary 6?
faq.a: Kinetic energy, potential energy (gravitational, elastic and chemical), light, heat, sound and electrical energy.
No. Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It is converted into other forms, often heat and sound, which are less useful.

faq.q: What energy does a battery store?
faq.a: A battery stores chemical potential energy, which is converted into electrical energy when it is used in a circuit.

items.q: Which form of energy does a battery mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: An object is lifted higher. What happens to its gravitational potential energy?
items.e: The higher it is, the more gravitational potential energy it has.

items.q: Which form of energy does a piece of charcoal for a barbecue mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: Where did the energy of the wind first come from?
items.e: The Sun heats the land and air unevenly, which causes wind.

items.q: Which form of energy is in a stretched rubber band?
items.e: Stretching stores energy.

items.q: Why do we need energy?
c: to move, grow and keep our bodies working
items.e: Living things need energy for life processes.

items.q: Which form of energy does the blades of a spinning fan mainly have?
items.e: It is moving.

items.q: What is energy?
c: the ability to do work or make things move or change
items.e: Energy makes things happen.

items.q: Which form of energy does a plate of chicken rice mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: Where did the energy in a chicken drumstick first come from?
items.e: The chicken ate plants, which got their energy from the Sun.

items.q: Which form of energy does water held behind a dam mainly have?
items.e: It is raised above the ground.

items.q: Which form of energy does the ringing of a school bell mainly have?
items.e: This is sound energy.

items.q: Which form of energy does a compressed spring in a toy mainly have?
items.e: It is stretched, bent or compressed.

items.q: Which form of energy does the bent bow of an archer, ready to shoot mainly have?
items.e: It is stretched, bent or compressed.

items.q: Which form of energy does the current in a wire to a lamp mainly have?
items.e: This is electrical energy.

items.q: Which form of energy is stored in food and batteries?
items.e: It is released when the food is used by the body or the battery is used.

items.q: Where did the energy in the rice we eat first come from?
items.e: The rice plant used light energy from the Sun to make food.

items.q: Can energy be created or destroyed?
c: No. It can only be converted from one form to another.
items.e: The total amount of energy stays the same.

items.q: Which form of energy does a moving object have?
items.e: The faster it moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

items.q: What is the main source of energy for the Earth?
items.e: Plants, animals, food and fuels all depend on the Sun.

items.q: An LED bulb and a filament bulb give the same amount of light. The LED bulb stays cooler. Why is the LED bulb better?
c: Less electrical energy is wasted as heat.
items.e: Less waste means less electricity used.

items.q: What happens to the kinetic energy of a cyclist who stops by braking?
c: It is converted mostly into heat energy in the brakes and wheels.
It turns into chemical potential energy in the bicycle.
items.e: The brakes get warm.

items.q: A pupil swings on a swing. At which point does she have the most kinetic energy?
c: at the lowest point of the swing
items.e: She moves fastest at the bottom.

items.q: Which energy conversion happens in a microphone?
items.e: It is the opposite of a speaker.

items.q: A solar panel makes electrical energy. Which form of energy goes into it?
items.e: A solar panel changes light into electrical energy.

items.q: Why does a light bulb get warm when it is switched on?
c: Some electrical energy is converted into heat energy, not just light energy.
Heat flows from the room into the bulb.
items.e: Bulbs give off light and heat.

items.q: A microphone changes sound into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a microphone is to make electrical energy.

items.q: Why does a swing slowly stop if no one pushes it?
c: Some energy is converted into heat and sound energy by friction and air resistance.
It runs out of potential energy forever.
items.e: Energy is converted into less useful forms.

items.q: A phone's ringer changes electrical energy into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a phone's ringer is to make sound.

items.q: A catapult shoots a stone. Which shows the main energy conversion?
items.e: A catapult shoots a stone: elastic potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: A wind turbine makes electrical energy. Which form of energy goes into it?
c: kinetic energy (something turns or moves it)
items.e: A wind turbine changes kinetic energy into electrical energy.

items.q: A toy car with a motor changes electrical energy into which main form of energy?
c: electrical energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a toy car with a motor is to make kinetic energy.

items.q: A pupil cycles up a slope and stops at the top. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → chemical potential energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
items.e: A pupil cycles up a slope and stops at the top: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy.

items.q: Water flows down from a dam and turns a generator. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: electrical energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: Water flows down from a dam and turns a generator: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy.

items.q: A wound-up toy car runs across the floor. Which shows the main energy conversion?
items.e: A wound-up toy car runs across the floor: elastic potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: A wind turbine turns to produce electricity. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: A wind turbine turns to produce electricity: kinetic energy → electrical energy.

items.q: A pupil swings on a swing. At which point does she have the most gravitational potential energy?
c: at the highest point of the swing
items.e: She is highest then.

items.q: A microphone makes electrical energy. Which form of energy goes into it?
items.e: A microphone changes sound into electrical energy.

items.q: Which energy conversion happens in a radio?
items.e: The speaker gives out sound.

items.q: A pupil rubs her hands together and they feel warm. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: A pupil rubs her hands together and they feel warm: kinetic energy → heat energy.

items.q: Why does Singapore install solar panels on HDB rooftops?
c: Solar panels create energy from nothing.
Sunlight is renewable and Singapore gets a lot of it.
items.e: Solar energy reduces the use of fuels.

items.q: A plant makes food in its leaves. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
items.e: A plant makes food in its leaves: light energy → chemical potential energy.

items.q: Which device changes electrical energy into kinetic energy?
items.e: Look at what goes in (electrical energy) and what comes out (kinetic energy).

items.q: Which form of energy does a ball rolling down a slope mainly have?
items.e: It is moving.

items.q: Where did the electricity from a solar panel first come from?
items.e: The solar panel converts light energy from the Sun.

items.q: A ball falls from a table to the floor. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
items.e: A ball falls from a table to the floor: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: Which device changes electrical energy into kinetic energy?
c: a toy car with a motor
items.e: Look at what goes in (electrical energy) and what comes out (kinetic energy).

items.q: Which form of energy does the warmth from a gas stove mainly have?
items.e: This is heat energy.

items.q: Where did the energy in petrol first come from?
items.e: Petrol comes from living things of long ago, which got their energy from the Sun.

items.q: Why should we switch off lights when we leave a room?
c: to save electrical energy and reduce the burning of fuels in power stations
to make the bulb cooler only
items.e: Most electricity in Singapore is made by burning natural gas.

items.q: Which device changes electrical energy into kinetic energy?
c: a bike light powered by the wheel
items.e: Look at what goes in (electrical energy) and what comes out (kinetic energy).

items.q: Which source of energy is renewable?
items.e: Sunlight will not run out; fossil fuels will.

items.q: Which device changes light into electrical energy?
items.e: Look at what goes in (light) and what comes out (electrical energy).

items.q: A battery powers a torch. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → chemical potential energy
chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
items.e: A battery powers a torch: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy.

items.q: Which form of energy does a moving MRT train mainly have?
items.e: It is moving.

items.q: Which form of energy does the glow of a torch mainly have?
items.e: This is light energy.

items.q: A pupil eats breakfast and then runs to school. Which shows the main energy conversion?
items.e: A pupil eats breakfast and then runs to school: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: Which energy conversion happens when a pupil plays the guitar?
items.e: The moving strings make sound.

items.q: What happens to the energy of a falling coconut just before it hits the ground?
c: Most of its gravitational potential energy has been converted into kinetic energy.
It has gained gravitational potential energy.
items.e: It speeds up as it falls.

items.q: Why does a toy car with a wound-up spring stop after a while?
c: Its elastic potential energy has all been converted into kinetic, heat and sound energy.
items.e: Energy changes form; it is not used up.

items.q: Which form of energy does a wound-up spring in a toy car mainly have?
items.e: It is stretched, bent or compressed.

items.q: Which device changes electrical energy into heat?
c: a bike light powered by the wheel
items.e: Look at what goes in (electrical energy) and what comes out (heat).

items.q: A solar panel powers a doorbell. Which shows the energy changes in order?
c: light energy → electrical energy → sound energy
sound energy → electrical energy → light energy
kinetic energy → electrical energy → heat energy
kinetic energy → electrical energy → light energy
items.e: Follow the energy from where it starts to where it ends.

items.q: A solar panel charges a battery that runs a fan. Which shows the energy changes in order?
c: light energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → kinetic energy
sound energy → electrical energy → kinetic energy
items.e: Follow the energy from where it starts to where it ends.

items.q: A TV screen changes electrical energy into which main form of energy?
c: electrical energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a TV screen is to make light.

items.q: A water wheel turns a generator that powers a light bulb. Which shows the energy changes in order?
c: kinetic energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → kinetic energy
light energy → electrical energy → sound energy
light energy → electrical energy → light energy
items.e: Follow the energy from where it starts to where it ends.

items.q: A wind turbine sends electricity to a lamp. Which shows the energy changes in order?
c: kinetic energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → kinetic energy
items.e: Follow the energy from where it starts to where it ends.

items.q: A solar panel on an HDB rooftop produces electricity. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
items.e: A solar panel on an HDB rooftop produces electricity: light energy → electrical energy.

items.q: A solar panel changes light into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a solar panel is to make electrical energy.

items.q: A battery runs a toy car's motor. Which shows the energy changes in order?
c: light energy → electrical energy → light energy
kinetic energy → electrical energy → sound energy
items.e: Follow the energy from where it starts to where it ends.

items.q: A speaker changes electrical energy into which main form of energy?
c: electrical energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a speaker is to make sound.

items.q: A solar calculator makes electrical energy. Which form of energy goes into it?
items.e: A solar calculator changes light into electrical energy.

items.q: A hand-crank torch makes light. Which form of energy goes into it?
c: kinetic energy (something turns or moves it)
items.e: A hand-crank torch changes kinetic energy into light.

items.q: A bike light powered by the wheel makes light. Which form of energy goes into it?
c: kinetic energy (something turns or moves it)
items.e: A bike light powered by the wheel changes kinetic energy into light.

items.q: Which device changes kinetic energy into electrical energy?
c: a toy car with a motor
items.e: Look at what goes in (kinetic energy) and what comes out (electrical energy).

items.q: A doorbell changes electrical energy into which main form of energy?
c: electrical energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a doorbell is to make sound.

items.q: A wind turbine charges a battery that runs a heater. Which shows the energy changes in order?
c: kinetic energy → electrical energy → heat energy
kinetic energy → electrical energy → light energy
heat energy → electrical energy → kinetic energy
items.e: Follow the energy from where it starts to where it ends.

items.q: Which device changes electrical energy into kinetic energy?
items.e: Look at what goes in (electrical energy) and what comes out (kinetic energy).

items.q: Which device changes electrical energy into sound?
items.e: Look at what goes in (electrical energy) and what comes out (sound).

items.q: Which form of energy does a running dog mainly have?
items.e: It is moving.

items.q: Which form of energy does petrol in a car's tank mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: A speaker changes electrical energy into
items.e: The speaker vibrates and makes sound.

items.q: Which form of energy does a book on a high shelf mainly have?
items.e: It is raised above the ground.

items.q: Which energy change happens when you rub your hands together?
items.e: Rubbing changes energy of kinetic energy into heat.

items.q: Siti released a toy car from different heights on a ramp and measured how far it travelled. What was she investigating?
c: how the starting height affects how far the car travels
items.e: A higher start gives more gravitational potential energy.

items.q: What does a generator do?
c: changes kinetic energy into electrical energy
items.e: Turning a generator, by hand, wind or water, makes electricity.

items.q: In Siti's experiment, which should be kept the same?
c: the time of the day only
the car and the surface of the ramp
items.e: Only the starting height should change.

c: Energy is destroyed when it hits the floor.
The ball gains energy from the floor.
Some energy is converted into heat and sound energy when it hits the floor.

items.q: What energy change happens in a battery-powered fan?
items.e: The motor spins the blades.

items.q: Which form of energy do solar panels take in?
items.e: Solar panels change light into electrical energy.

items.q: A pupil touched a bulb after it had been on for 10 minutes. It was hot. What can she conclude?
c: Light energy is the same as heat energy.
Some electrical energy was converted into heat energy.
The bulb creates heat from nothing.
items.e: Bulbs waste some energy as heat.

items.q: What does it mean to convert energy?
c: to change energy from one form into another
items.e: A lamp converts electrical energy into light.

items.q: Ravi stretched a rubber band by different lengths to launch a paper ball. The ball went further when the band was stretched more. Why?
c: More elastic potential energy was stored and converted into kinetic energy.
items.e: More stretch stores more energy.

items.q: A hand-crank radio is turned to play music. Which shows the energy changes in order?
c: kinetic energy → electrical energy → sound energy
sound energy → electrical energy → kinetic energy
kinetic energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → kinetic energy
items.e: Follow the energy from where it starts to where it ends.

items.q: Mei Ling recorded the temperature of two bulbs giving the same light: Bulb A 80 °C, Bulb B 35 °C. Which bulb wastes less energy as heat?
items.e: The cooler bulb converts less electrical energy into heat.

items.q: Can a device make energy from nothing?
c: No. It changes energy that goes into it into other forms.
Yes, if it is turned on.
items.e: Energy is changed, not made from nothing.
